summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and require
details: The package ships a beacon.cjs that POSTs a JSON payload containing os.hostname(), __dirname (install path), process.cwd(), the package name, and the Node version to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. The beacon fires automatically from two triggers: the package.json postinstall script invokes `node beacon.cjs`, and the declared main index.js calls `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` at top level and then re-exports a Proxy returning no-op functions for every property so consuming bundlers do not crash on the empty surface. The destination is a bare IP, not any publisher or vendor domain, is not caller-configurable, and the package exposes no legitimate functionality — the shipped surface exists solely to leak internal hostnames and build paths of any environment that resolves this name, the canonical dependency-confusion reconnaissance shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
